# Elevance Health (ELV) Q2 2025 earnings summary
## Q2 2025 earnings summary
### Executive summary
- Adjusted diluted EPS was $8.84, with GAAP diluted EPS at $7.72; full-year 2025 adjusted EPS guidance revised to approximately $30.00 due to elevated medical cost trends in ACA and slower Medicaid rate alignment.
- Net income for Q2 2025 was $1.74 billion, down 24.2% year-over-year, mainly due to higher medical costs and lower Health Benefits margins.
- Returned $2.0 billion to shareholders year-to-date through share repurchases and dividends.
- Strategic focus remains on cost management, targeted investments, and operational discipline to stabilize margins and support long-term growth.
### Financial highlights
- Benefit expense ratio increased to 88.9% in Q2 2025, up 260 bps year-over-year, reflecting higher medical costs in Medicaid and ACA plans.
- Operating expense ratio improved to 10.1% (adjusted: 10.0%), down 140–160 bps year-over-year.
### Outlook and guidance
- Full-year 2025 adjusted EPS guidance revised to approximately $30.00, reflecting persistent elevated trends in ACA and Medicaid.
- Benefit expense ratio forecasted at ~90% for 2025.
- More earnings expected in Q3 than Q4, with Q4 impacted by anticipated utilization surge if enhanced subsidies expire.

"In the second quarter, Elevance Health made meaningful progress in delivering an experience that is simple and personal to those we serve, while advancing our efforts to enhance efficiency across the healthcare system. We are updating our outlook to reflect elevated medical cost trends in ACA and slower rate alignment in Medicaid. While the external environment continues to evolve, we are focused on the areas within our control - managing healthcare costs, deploying targeted investments in advanced technology and value-based care delivery, and reinforcing the operational foundation that supports long-term value creation. With the embedded earnings power of our diversified Health Benefits and Carelon businesses, we remain confident in achieving at least 12% average annual growth in adjusted diluted EPS over time."

President and Chief Executive Officer

Elevance Health reported $1.7 billion in profit during the second quarter, down 24% from Q2 2024, which was enough to drive shares in the company down slightly this week.
The insurer brought in $2.3 billion in profit in Q2 last year. The lower performance this year resulted in $8.84 in earnings per share, with the Associated Press reporting this fell short of Wall Street’s expectations, with investors anticipating $9.16 per share.
Profits are also down mid-year compared to last year. Elevance has earned $3.9 billion in profit so far this year, a 13.6% decrease from the roughly $4.5 billion it tallied through the first six months of 2024.
Though profits were down, Elevance did overperform on revenue; while analysts had predicted $48.2 billion in revenue, the company posted $49.8 billion in revenue, a 13% increase over Q2 2024.
CEO Gail Boudreaux attributed this performance to higher costs in the Affordable Care Act’s marketplaces, as well as elevated Medicaid costs.
“We are updating our outlook to reflect elevated medical cost trends in ACA and slower rate alignment in Medicaid,” said Boudreaux. “While the external environment continues to evolve, we are focused on the areas within our control - managing healthcare costs, deploying targeted investments in advanced technology and value-based care delivery, and reinforcing the operational foundation that supports long-term value creation.”

01—Abstract

## Summary

Summary of the 8-K filed July 17, 2025. Cited figures are marked; the original filing is the authoritative source.

Elevance Health (ELV) reported second quarter 2025 results on July 17, 2025, with operating revenue of $49.4 billiona, up **14.3%** year over year, driven by higher Health Benefits premium yields, acquisitions, and Medicare Advantage growth.

However, profitability weakened sharply: the benefit expense ratio rose 260 basis points to **88.9%** on elevated medical cost trend in Medicaid and ACA plans, operating gain fell **12.3%** to $2.4 billionb, and GAAP diluted EPS dropped **21.6%** to **$7.72** (adjusted EPS **$8.84**, down **14.2%**). Health Benefits operating margin compressed to **3.8%** from **5.8%**, while Carelon was a bright spot, with segment revenue up **36%** and operating gain up **33%**. Management revised its full-year 2025 outlook, now expecting GAAP diluted EPS of approximately **$24.10** and adjusted diluted EPS of approximately **$30.00**.

Management attributed the revision to elevated cost trends in ACA and slower rate alignment in Medicaid, and reiterated a long-term target of at least **12%** average annual adjusted EPS growth. Cash generation was solid, with year-to-date operating cash flow of $3.1 billionc (**0.8x** GAAP net income), and the company returned **$2.0 billion** to shareholders year to date through buybacks and dividends, with about **$8.0 billion** of repurchase authorization remaining.

The key investor takeaway is that the quarter reflects a cost-trend problem in the core Health Benefits business that offset strong top-line growth and Carelon expansion. Investors should focus on whether medical cost trends in Medicaid and ACA stabilize, the pace of Medicaid rate alignment, and the durability of the revised earnings guidance.

•2Q 2025 operating revenue of $49.4 billion, up 14.3% from 2Q 2024

•Revising FY 2025 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to approximately $30.00

Indianapolis, IN - July 17, 2025 - Elevance Health, Inc. (NYSE: ELV) reported second quarter 2025 results.
"In the second quarter, Elevance Health made meaningful progress in delivering an experience that is simple and personal to those we serve, while advancing our efforts to enhance efficiency across the healthcare system. We are updating our outlook to reflect elevated medical cost trends in ACA and slower rate alignment in Medicaid. While the external environment continues to evolve, we are focused on the areas within our control - managing healthcare costs, deploying targeted investments in advanced technology and value-based care delivery, and reinforcing the operational foundation that supports long-term value creation. With the embedded earnings power of our diversified Health Benefits and Carelon businesses, we remain confident in achieving at least 12% average annual growth in adjusted diluted EPS over time."
Gail K. Boudreaux
President and Chief Executive Officer
Given the ongoing and industry-wide impact of elevated cost trends in ACA and Medicaid, Elevance Health now expects 2025 GAAP net income per diluted share to be approximately $24.10 and adjusted net income per diluted share to be approximately $30.00.
